findings.title: High-cost rules are marked Always
findings.impact: Maximum activation cost is paid on every task.
findings.recommended_action: Convert to Agent Requested, Auto Attached, or an explicit skill after behavioral review.

findings.title: Always activation footprint requires per-rule justification
findings.evidence: 40 of 61 rules (66%) resolve to always activation.
findings.impact: Broad persistent context can create instruction collisions and consume agent context.
findings.recommended_action: Review each Always rule; keep only short non-negotiable governance and irreversible-action constraints.

findings.title: Rules exceed the 500-line hard target
findings.impact: Very large rule payloads raise context and contradiction risk.
findings.recommended_action: Split immediately behind stable IDs and preserve compatibility aliases where required.

findings.title: Oversized active rules should be split or converted to procedures
findings.impact: Large rules are expensive to attach and harder to keep internally consistent.
findings.recommended_action: Move multi-step procedures to skills/commands and keep persistent rule contracts focused.

findings.title: Most legacy rules still use derived compatibility IDs
findings.evidence: 53 rules lack an explicit immutable frontmatter ID.
findings.impact: Renames cannot be distinguished reliably from replacement or deletion.
findings.recommended_action: Add explicit IDs when rules are materially edited; do not mass-rewrite solely for metadata.

findings.title: Deprecated rules remain in the active rule directory
findings.impact: Compatibility content can still be discovered or explicitly referenced.
findings.recommended_action: Retain only with a documented compatibility reason and removal plan.

convergence.note: No corpus-wide activation changes were made automatically; findings require evidence-backed review.
